stories.text: As a **nuclear medicine physician**, I want PET values in Bq/ml and SUV (body weight; later lean body mass) from the DICOM PET module (units, decay correction, radiopharmaceutical dose and time, half-life, patient weight), refused with the reason when data are missing, so that numbers mean what they say.
As a **physician**, I want SUVmax, SUVpeak (1 cm³ sphere), SUVmean, MTV and TLG of a segment, and thresholds at 41 % of SUVmax and at SUV ≥ 2.5, so that a PET report needs no other tool.

As a **reader**, I want PET colour maps (inverted grey, hot/inferno) and SUV windows (0–5, 0–10, 0–15) in slices and MIP, with HU presets hidden for PET and MR; a shader change with CPU parity and a visual check (L1).

As an **agent developer**, I want `value_unit` = `SUVbw` or `Bq/ml` in the agent with the PET metrics in `segment metrics`, identical over CLI and MCP, and identifiers (weight, dose times) kept out of outputs unless allowed.

As a **reader**, I want a PET volume shown in colour over a CT of the same study on the common LPS geometry, with opacity and its own window, marked "not registered" (no alignment is claimed, as in 19.9-b).
As a **reader**, I want the probe and the segment metrics to read the volume I choose (CT in HU, PET in SUV) under the same cursor.
As an **agent developer**, I want `view slice` and `view mpr` to render the overlay so that an agent sees what the person sees.

criteria.text: `ferrum-domain` has no I/O/GPU/UI dependencies. `ferrum-app` compiles without wgpu and egui. Dependencies point inward (see `docs/architecture.md`).

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want a layered workspace (domain, processing, io, render, app, viewer) so that I can change the UI, file formats or GPU backend independently.

criteria.text: Application tests run against an in-memory repository and a recording GPU sink.

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want storage and GPU access behind ports (`VolumeRepository`, `GpuSink`) so that use cases can be tested without files or a graphics card.

criteria.text: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `FERRUM_REQUIRE_GPU=1` tests on lavapipe, and a release build.

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want CI that checks formatting, lints, tests on a software GPU and a release build so that regressions are caught before merge.

criteria.text: ADRs in `docs/decisions/` (Rust + wgpu + egui; canonical LPS frame).

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want recorded architecture decisions so that the reasons behind the design survive.

criteria.text: Recursive scan, grouping by Series Instance UID, and a series picker when a folder holds more than one series.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to open a DICOM folder and have it split into series so that I can pick the study I need.

criteria.text: Sorted by projection on the plane normal, with fallbacks to Instance Number and Slice Location. Covered by tests.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want slices ordered by their real position so that anatomy is never shuffled.

criteria.text: Explicit/implicit VR, big endian, JPEG, JPEG 2000, RLE, deflate, multi-frame, signed pixels, rescale slope/intercept, MONOCHROME1 and colour. Each case is covered by a test that generates the file at run time.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want compressed and unusual DICOM to open so that I don't have to convert files.

criteria.text: NIfTI-1 reader with gzip. `sform`/`qform` are honoured and the volume is reoriented to LPS. A 4D file shows its first volume.

stories.text: As a **researcher**, I want to open `.nii` / `.nii.gz` so that I can inspect public datasets.

criteria.text: Parallel decode (rayon), a progress overlay and a cancel button. A 512×512×252 CT loads in about 0.34 s on 4 CPU cores.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want loading to be fast and cancellable, with progress, so that large studies never freeze the app.

criteria.text: Drag-and-drop overlay, CLI arguments, **Open folder** / **Open files**, and Ctrl+O.

stories.text: As a **user**, I want to drop files onto the window or pass them on the command line so that opening a study takes one gesture.

criteria.text: A DICOM series with more than one image at a slice position (echoes, b-values, phases, frames) loads one volume, never a mix: at every position the image that sorts first by Temporal Position Identifier, Echo Number, Diffusion b-value, Acquisition Number, Trigger Time, Instance Number, file order; this holds for files in any order and for 2 echoes interleaved by Instance Number. ✅ (PR 1)
Such a load warns with the number of images per position (`k`, or `min–max` when positions differ) and the number of positions, and says that one volume of several is shown. ✅ (PR 1)

When a gap between neighbouring positions differs from the median gap by more than max(0.01 mm, 2 % of the median), the load warns with the smallest and largest gap and the median used for the slice spacing; a regular series (also 1 mm or 5 mm, any orientation) gives no warning. ✅ (PR 1)

A series ordered without image positions (Instance Number, Slice Location, file order), or a multi-frame file whose per-frame positions are not read, warns that the slice spacing comes from the header (with the value); a series of several multi-frame files warns that only the first frame of each is read; a series without Pixel Spacing warns that 1 mm is assumed. ✅ (PR 1)
A NIfTI file with more than one volume (`dim[4..7]`) warns that volume 1 of N is shown; a 3D file gives no warning. ✅ (PR 1)
The agent's `study open` and `study info` carry every load warning in the envelope `warnings`, identical over CLI and MCP; the warnings hold no identifiers (privacy scan). ✅ (PR 1)
The desktop app shows the load warnings once after loading (a window the person dismisses) and keeps them in the series information. ✅ (PR 1)

Without a window stored in the data and without `window`, agent renders use the same percentile window (0.5–99.5 %) as the desktop app, from one implementation in `ferrum-domain`; a stored DICOM window or an explicit `window` is used as before. ✅ (PR 2)

stories.text: As a **clinician** reading MR or PET, I want the loader to tell me when a series could not be shown as stored (several images per slice position, a 4D file, irregular or unknown slice spacing) so that I never measure a mixed or distorted volume without knowing.

criteria.text: A DICOM series (classic or Enhanced) is stored in the canonical LPS grid, as NIfTI already is: its voxel axes are permuted and flipped onto the closest of `+x` left, `+y` posterior, `+z` superior; an oblique remainder stays in the direction; every voxel keeps its value at its patient position (exact for sagittal, coronal, axial with reversed rows, normal towards the feet, and 20° oblique). ✅
The axial view of a sagittal series shows axial anatomy, and the screen's left is the patient's right in every view, as for an axial CT. ✅
Probe, measurements and patient coordinates give the same millimetres as before for the same anatomical point. ✅

A DICOM SEG of such a series lies on the LPS grid; a frame references a source image only when it lies in that image's plane, otherwise the whole source series is referenced without per-frame derivation. ✅

stories.text: As a **clinician** reading a sagittal or coronal MR (or any DICOM series not acquired head-to-feet axially), I want its planes shown as what they are, with true left and right, so that I never read a mirrored or mislabelled image.

criteria.text: Slices are sampled on the GPU from the 3D texture. A slice change takes about 4 ms. Nearest or linear sampling.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want axial, coronal and sagittal slices rendered straight from the volume so that switching planes is instant.

criteria.text: Mouse drag, L/W fields, presets (full range, brain, soft tissue, lung, bone) and auto percentiles.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want window/level by drag, by numeric input and by preset so that I can read soft tissue, lung and bone.

criteria.text: Ctrl+wheel zooms at the cursor. Double-click resets the view.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want pan and zoom around the cursor so that I can inspect details.

criteria.text: 2×2 layout (three planes + 3D). Crosshairs are colour-coded per plane. Right-click moves every plane to that point.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want an MPR layout with linked crosshairs so that I can localise a finding in three planes.

criteria.text: All data is in LPS. Edge labels show R/L, A/P, S/I, verified against NIfTI and DICOM of the same patient.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to see correct patient orientation so that I never mix up left and right.

criteria.text: The probe shows voxel indices and the rescaled value.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want a voxel probe so that I can read physical values (HU).

criteria.text: Results are in mm, mm² and degrees and account for anisotropic voxels. Tool state machines are unit-tested.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want distance, angle, area, rectangle and text tools so that I can document findings.

criteria.text: Move and delete tools, plus "Clear all". Annotations are bound to their slice.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to move, delete and clear annotations so that I can fix mistakes.

criteria.text: Four techniques in one WGSL ray caster, specialised through a pipeline-overridable constant.

stories.text: As a **clinician**, I want tissue, isosurface, MIP and transfer-function rendering so that I can choose the best view of the anatomy.

criteria.text: Empty-space skipping over a brick grid, lower resolution while rotating, and jittered ray starts. The isosurface on the 512×512×252 CT runs at about 20 fps even on a software GPU.

stories.text: As a **clinician**, I want smooth interaction on large studies so that exploring in 3D feels natural.

criteria.text: Gradient Phong shading, bisection refinement of surface hits, and a precomputed AO volume.

stories.text: As a **clinician**, I want shaded surfaces with ambient occlusion so that depth is easy to read.

criteria.text: Trackball, pan, zoom and reset. One-click A/P/L/R/S/I views. An orientation gizmo.

stories.text: As a **clinician**, I want to rotate, pan, zoom and jump to standard views so that I can orient myself quickly.

criteria.text: The CPU ray caster mirrors `volume.wgsl`. GPU parity tests cover every mode and feature.

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want a CPU reference ray caster so that GPU output can be verified pixel by pixel.

criteria.text: Automatic box downsampling to `max_texture_dimension_3d`. `R16Float` fallback when `R16Unorm` is not filterable.

stories.text: As a **user**, I want volumes larger than my GPU's limit to still open so that the app never fails on big data.

criteria.text: Log-scaled histogram. Drag points, double-click to add, right-click to remove, and a per-point colour picker.

stories.text: As a **clinician**, I want to edit the transfer function over the histogram so that I can highlight the structures I need.

criteria.text: *Soft tissue + bone*, *lung vessels* and *bone* presets that adapt to the data range.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want CT presets in Hounsfield units so that typical views need one click.

criteria.text: Up to 8 analytic half-spaces. Optional raw-slice overlay on the cut surface. Reset button.

stories.text: As a **surgeon**, I want a clip box, a view-aligned cut and an oblique plane so that I can expose internal structures.

criteria.text: Cylindrical brush with radius and depth in mm. Undo (Ctrl+Z) and restore all. Incremental mask upload to the GPU.

stories.text: As a **surgeon**, I want to erase occluding anatomy (e.g. the scanner table) with a brush so that I can present a clean view.

criteria.text: Filters run as background jobs, and the UI stays responsive.

stories.text: As a **researcher**, I want Gaussian smoothing and Sobel edges so that I can reduce noise or emphasise boundaries.

criteria.text: NIfTI writer with a correct `sform`, round-trip tested. PNG screenshot of the window.

stories.text: As a **researcher**, I want NIfTI export and PNG screenshots so that I can reuse results elsewhere.

criteria.text: An Info window lists the series attributes.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to see the DICOM attributes of the series so that I can check acquisition parameters.

criteria.text: Full-bleed dark canvas. Glass docks: modes and planes on the left, tools in the centre, file actions on the right. Status HUD at the bottom.

stories.text: As a **user**, I want the image to take the whole screen, with controls in floating docks, so that nothing competes with the anatomy.

criteria.text: **Tab** toggles the panel. Slices and Volume tabs in MPR. Collapsible sections.

stories.text: As a **user**, I want a collapsible settings panel with only the relevant controls so that the screen stays uncluttered.

criteria.text: Corner brackets in the plane colour. Monospace HUD labels. A slice scrubber on the view edge.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want HUD read-outs in the views (plane, slice number, W/L, zoom, orientation) so that I don't have to look away from the image.

criteria.text: The recent list persists in the user config directory (8 entries). UI tests cover the start screen.

stories.text: As a **user**, I want a start screen with drag-and-drop and recent studies so that I can reopen my work in one click.

criteria.text: Every dock button has a tooltip and an accessible label. `egui_kittest` drives the real app by those labels.

stories.text: As a **user**, I want icon buttons with tooltips and accessible names so that the UI is both compact and testable.

criteria.text: About 180 tests: unit, property-based, data layer, shader validation, GPU parity, application and UI. See `docs/testing.md`.

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want a layered test suite so that every change is checked at the right level.

criteria.text: `make bench`, `make snapshot` (timings per technique) and `make showcase` (README images from public data).

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want reproducible benchmarks and screenshots so that performance and visuals can be compared over time.

criteria.text: README: gallery from the MSD lung CT, supported modalities and grid limits, performance numbers with the test hardware, and references to the visualization literature.

stories.text: As a **visitor**, I want a README with real-data screenshots, limits and performance numbers so that I can judge the project quickly.

criteria.text: The product is **FERRUM**, "High-performance medical imaging". Crates are `ferrum-*`, the binary is `ferrum`, and environment variables use the `FERRUM_` prefix (ADR 0004). The logo is the "Fe" tile of the periodic table.

stories.text: As a **visitor**, I want the project to have a clear name and tagline so that I remember what it is.

criteria.text: Navy surfaces, one blue accent, light-grey read-outs over a black canvas. No glow or saturated decorations.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want a calm interface that does not compete with the images during long reading sessions.

criteria.text: The header holds the study, the 2D/3D/MPR switch and file actions. The toolbar holds the tools of the current mode. The right panel has *Image*, *Volume* and *Details* tabs, and a status bar sits at the bottom.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want a predictable workstation layout so that every control is always in the same place.

criteria.text: A *Studies* sidebar shows the current study and the recently opened ones. One click opens a study.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to switch between recent studies without a file dialog.

criteria.text: *Window* and *Level* rows with a slider and an editable value. Presets and *Auto* are chips.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want window and level as sliders with exact values, besides presets.

criteria.text: **Info** opens the *Details* tab: dimensions, spacing, intensity range and DICOM attributes.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want the series attributes next to the image, not in a pop-up.

criteria.text: `cargo-llvm-cov` job in CI that counts all test levels. lcov and HTML reports are kept as artifacts, a summary is shown on the run page, and the job fails below the floor (87 %; baseline 88.5 % of lines). `make coverage` produces the report locally.

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want test coverage measured on every pull request so that untested code is visible and coverage never silently drops.

criteria.text: Clippy enforces cognitive complexity ≤ 25, ≤ 120 lines per function and nesting ≤ 6 (`clippy.toml`). Functions that exceeded it were split: the slice view, the start screen, the series picker and NIfTI reorientation.

stories.text: As a **developer**, I want a complexity budget so that functions stay small and readable.

stories.text: As a **maintainer**, I want the release to be cut without pushing tags so that it works from any environment.

criteria.text: In the 2D view, the *Image* tab lists every annotation with type, value, plane and slice number. The list is not shown in 3D/MPR. Each row can be deleted.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to see all annotations of the study in one list so that I can review my findings.

criteria.text: Each annotation stores its plane and slice. Clicking the row (or its arrow) switches the 2D view to that plane and slice. Rows on the current slice are highlighted.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to jump to the slice of an annotation so that I can find it again instantly.

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want to name annotations so that a measurement says what it measures.

Covered by io, application and UI tests.

stories.text: As a **researcher**, I want to export annotations to JSON so that I can analyse them elsewhere and link them to the study.

criteria.text: Slice numbers are one-based in the slider, on the image, in the annotation list and in the export (`slice_number`; `slice_index` stays zero-based for tools).

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want one slice numbering everywhere so that numbers never disagree.

criteria.text: Smoothing and edge filters are hidden from the UI: they changed the data irreversibly. The processing code stays available for future use.

stories.text: As a **clinician**, I want only clinically useful tools so that the interface stays focused.

criteria.text: `docs/engine-protocol.md` (`ferrum-engine/1`) and ADR 0007. ✅

stories.text: As an **integrator**, I want a documented engine protocol so that I can plug any segmentation engine into FERRUM without changing its code.

criteria.text: Volume geometry (origin, direction). `LabelMap`, segments with name, colour, visibility, opacity and volume in ml. 2D fill and outline and 3D rendering, with CPU-reference parity. NIfTI label-map import and export. ✅

stories.text: As a **radiologist**, I want segments shown over the image and in 3D so that I can review a segmentation.

stories.text: As an **integrator**, I want a documented skill design so that I can plan FERRUM into my agent harness.

criteria.text: `ferrum-agent` + `ferrum-cli`: study, view (slice, MPR, montage, 3D with pixel mapping), probe, stats, profile, measure, annotate, segment (incl. threshold region growing), export. criteria.text: The reference value is the median of the smoothed values around the seed, so a noisy seed voxel does not decide (a 200 HU outlier at the seed of a 60 HU organ still yields ≥ 3 500 of the 4 096 voxels);
with ±40 HU noise a 16³ organ phantom is segmented to 3 500–4 300 voxels and a vessel crossing it is filled, also when it leaves the organ through its surface;
a 1 mm bridge to a second structure is cut by an opening of 1.5 mm and leaks without it;
a lesion 3 mm wide survives an opening of 3 mm unchanged (27 voxels);

smoothing of 1 mm does not shrink a sharp-edged ball (895 voxels with and without smoothing, opening and hole filling; strong smoothing recovers only the outermost boundary layer and shrinks small structures — stated in the panel hint);
smoothing and opening are in millimetres: on 5 mm slices a bridge 4 mm wide and one slice thick is cut by an opening of 3 mm and leaks without it;
when the click is not in the core left by the opening (a thin spot), the core nearest to the click survives, never a larger organ elsewhere;
the default tolerance is a tenth of the window width, at most 40 (the automatic window of a whole CT is over 1 000 wide and would leak on the first click);

the click grows the region on a worker thread: the click returns at once (`Viewer::region_pending`), the segment appears when the job finishes; a second click meanwhile is refused with a message and starts no job; *Cancel* (or clearing the segmentation, or opening another study) stops it and no segment is created even if the job had just finished; voxels labelled since the click are never overwritten; the cancel flag is checked every 65 536 grown voxels and between the later steps;

the tolerance is chosen at every click until the user sets it: 300 for an aerated seed (below −500 in a CT-like volume), otherwise as in 16.6-l; the panel shows the value used and a checkbox *Automatic tolerance*; moving the slider switches it off (on MSD lung CT the default of 40 grew nothing and ±200…±400 gives Dice 0.92–0.97 against the lung of the click; field test, `docs/testing.md`);

on real CT the default settings give Dice ≥ 0.90 against the reference on MSD Task03 liver cases (field test; measured on four cases: 0.951, 0.961, 0.958 and 0.883 — the last because the reference includes a hypodense tumour at the surface; see `docs/testing.md`);

the failures are told apart: seed outside the grid, seed already in a segment, region larger than the limit (message names the limit, the tolerance and the opening); the default limit is 8 000 ml (a lung is about 6 000 ml);
a seed on an edge or a vessel is never rejected (the region always contains the seed; "too large" is reported only for the size limit);
the panel offers smoothing (0–6 mm), bridge cutting (0–15 mm), hole filling and a size limit up to 20 000 ml.

Content: **GLCM** (Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix) — how often pairs of voxels with given grey levels sit at a given distance and direction; contrast, homogeneity, correlation. **GLRLM** (Gray Level Run Length Matrix) — lengths of runs of equal grey level along a direction; coarse versus fine texture. **GLSZM** (Gray Level Size Zone Matrix) — sizes of connected zones of equal grey level; zone heterogeneity, direction-independent. **GLDM** (Gray Level Dependence Matrix) — how many neighbours share a voxel's grey level within a tolerance; local uniformity. **NGTDM** (Neighbouring Gray Tone Difference Matrix) — difference between a voxel and the mean of its neighbourhood; coarseness, busyness, complexity.

criteria.text: `docs/gpu-sharing.md` specifies the protocol `ferrum-gpu-lock/1`: directory, file names per group and holder, the OS lock used (`flock` on Unix, `LockFileEx` on Windows), the holder record (holder name, process id, leased MiB, start time; no study data), how to acquire and release, the timeout, and stale holders.
A permissive crate `ferrum-gpu-lock` (MIT OR Apache-2.0, no FERRUM crate, only `rustix` on Unix for the user id) implements it, and `ferrum-agent` uses it instead of its own `GpuLock`.

The lock directory is per user: `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/ferrum/gpu` on Linux, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ferrum\gpu` on Windows, or `network.gpu_lock_dir`; it is created with mode 0700 (without `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`: `~/.cache/ferrum/gpu`). A directory or lock file owned by another user, or a directory that group or others can write, is refused with an error that names the path; FERRUM never falls back to `/tmp`.

Two-process test: an external holder holds the group; `segment auto` (mock engine) waits and succeeds within 1 s after the holder releases. When the holder is killed (`SIGKILL`) instead, the call goes ahead within 1 s.

A wait longer than `engine_job_timeout_s` ends with `engine_unavailable`, naming the holder and its lease; over MCP the wait reports progress ("waiting for GPU group card: llama-server holds 6 144 MiB").
A group without a capacity (23.2-d) behaves as today: one holder at a time, external holders included.

stories.text: As a **harness developer**, I want a documented GPU-group lock that my own process can take so that my model server and FERRUM's engines never use the card at the same time beyond its size.

criteria.text: A holder takes a lease of N MiB. An engine call of the group goes ahead only when the leases of the live holders plus its expected peak fit in the group's capacity; otherwise it waits as in 23.1-d/e. FERRUM's own engine calls of a group still run one at a time (rule 1 of §2).

The expected peak of an engine comes from the operator (`network.gpu_peaks_mib`) and from the engine's `GET /v1/info` (`limits.expected_peak_mib`, optional, additive to `ferrum-engine/1`). The engine's value may raise the operator's but never lower it (the effective peak is the larger). An engine with neither takes the whole group.
Test: capacity 12 000 MiB with a 6 000 MiB lease. A call with a 7 000 MiB peak waits, then goes ahead once the lease is released; a call with a 4 000 MiB peak goes ahead at once.
The capacity of a group is set by the operator (`network.gpu_capacity_mib`). An expected peak larger than the capacity runs only when the group has no other holder, with a warning.
Lock records and outputs pass the identifier scan; no study path, UID or name is written to the lock directory.

stories.text: As an **operator**, I want a holder to declare how much of the card it holds so that FERRUM runs an engine next to a resident model when it fits, and waits when it does not.

criteria.text: The desktop app reads the operator's `[network]` GPU settings from the same configuration file as the agent and takes the lease for an engine of a group before every request that may use the GPU.
While it waits, the AI panel shows "Waiting for GPU: <holder> (pid N) holds M MiB (group G)" with Cancel. Cancel releases nothing it does not hold, and the request is not sent.
UI test: an external holder makes the panel show the waiting state, and releasing it lets the request run.

stories.text: As a **clinician** using the desktop app's AI tools, I want them to take the same GPU group as the agent so that the viewer never starts an engine next to a model that leaves no room.

criteria.text: After the last session of the nnInteractive bridge closes (`DELETE` or TTL expiry), the bridge's GPU memory falls to its weights-only level ± 200 MiB, measured with `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` on the user's card (field). A bridge unit test checks that both paths drop the image and empty the cache.

A bridge that supports it reports `capabilities.unload: true` and serves `POST /v1/unload` (additive to `ferrum-engine/1`, in the conformance suite). The endpoint is refused with `busy` while a session or job is active. Afterwards the bridge holds no GPU memory at all (no CUDA context, measured), and its next session reloads the model; the reload time is measured and documented.

`engine unload [--engine URL | --group G]` asks every idle bridge (of the group) to unload. The output lists, per engine, `unloaded`, `busy` or `unsupported`; it never stops a running job. CLI and MCP give identical JSON, and the schema, `commands.json`, docs and contract tests are updated.

`GET /v1/info` may report `resident_mib` (optional), and `engine list` shows it per engine marked as reported by the engine. The docs say that a holder checks free memory itself (NVML) instead of trusting it (point 7 of #68).

stories.text: As an **operator**, I want idle bridges to give their GPU memory back, completely when asked, and to see what each bridge holds, so that a 12 GB card has room for TotalSegmentator `total` (about 10 GB guided) next to a resident model.

criteria.text: `scripts/benchmark_engines.py --external-holder "<command>" --lease-mib N` starts the holder, samples GPU memory during every step, and reports the combined peak and the time each call waited.

Field run on the user's card with the harness's `llama-server` and nnInteractive plus TotalSegmentator: 20 engine calls in Demo 2's order without CUDA out-of-memory errors. Rule 2 of §2 is updated to what the bridge does, and a new ADR (0015) records the lock protocol, the crate and the lease.

An operator without the harness can wrap a sidecar: `ferrum-cli gpu hold --group G --lease-mib N -- <command>` holds the lease while the command runs and releases it when the command exits; it is never an MCP tool.

criteria.text: `check_source` canonicalises the returned path and every read root before comparing: a symlink inside a root that points outside it is refused with `forbidden` — as a file, as a folder, through the link. A root named through a symlink grants exactly its target. The check judges exactly the spelling that is returned and that the reader opens (`.` and `..` resolved lexically): a `..` behind a depth-changing link must not split the checked path from the opened one (security review).
`resolve_workspace` holds the same boundary against `workspace_root`; a workspace that does not exist yet still resolves.

`Study::load` scans the checked source path and re-checks every recorded file path of the manifest before hashing or scanning it; a manifest path with a `..` component is refused outright (the check normalises it lexically, but `verify_sources`, the cache stamps and the DICOM export open the raw spelling in filesystem order — behind a symlink the two diverge; legitimate manifests never hold one). A crafted `workspace.json` cannot point the load outside the roots.

`collect_files` does not follow the symlinks it discovers while descending (folder and file links are skipped; on Windows junctions too — std marks them symlinks, pinned by a test); explicitly passed paths are honoured as before; a link loop terminates.
The walk is bounded: depth ≤ 8 and ≤ 100 000 entries (the harness guard's numbers). Exceeding either is refused with `limit` (`RepositoryError::Limit`, additive), never silently cut (L37).

criteria.text: The generator parses every `## Stage N` section of a fixture plan: number, title, heading marker (✅/🚧/📋), story rows `N.k`, criteria `[N.k-x]` with inline ✅ and PR references; struck-through criteria (``) are excluded; letter stages (F1/F2), the Roadmap's draft stages (`### Stage N`) and early stages whose criteria carry no IDs parse as story-level units with the heading's marker; Implementation tables are recognised by their header and their rows are not stories; the parsed structure equals an exact expected fixture.

Lifecycle is derived per criterion and per stage from two revisions: `released` when done at the latest `v*` tag reachable from `origin/main`; `develop` when done at the target revision but not at the tag (or no done evidence at the tag); `progress` when not done and the heading is 🚧; `planned` when not done and the heading is 📋; done means an inline ✅ or a ✅ heading. A fixture repository (tag + target) yields exact buckets, including a lagging heading (stage 🚧, criterion ✅ with a merged PR → criterion `develop`); a stage's bucket is `unknown` > `progress` > `develop` > `released` > `planned` over its criteria, and its counts per bucket are exact.

A criterion's verification reuses the `ferrum-analyze` convention: code files citing `covers N.k-x` (the same extensions and skipped directories) and docs validation-table rows naming the ID with `visual`/`field`/`manual`; the output names the citing files and levels.

The crate graph comes from `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` (fallback: the workspace `Cargo.toml` when cargo is unavailable): nodes are the workspace crates with their `description`, edges the intra-workspace dependencies; the declared layering (CLAUDE.md) is checked — dependencies point inward through the tier table, with the documented same-tier pairs and the per-crate prohibitions (`ferrum-app` without wgpu/egui, `ferrum-agent`'s closed dependency list without wgpu/egui, `ferrum-ui` without eframe/rfd, `ferrum-view` without egui, `ferrum-gpu-lock` standalone); every violating edge is named; a crate changed since the release tag is marked.

Output is deterministic and clean: two runs on the same inputs produce byte-identical `data.json` (sorted keys; the stamp — source SHAs, tag, target commit date — is derived from git, not the wall clock, and lives in one `meta` block); no absolute machine path (drive letter, `/home/`, `/Users/`, `/mnt/`) appears anywhere in the output.

The generator refuses to guess: an unknown heading marker or a story row without criteria under a ✅/🚧 heading produces a named warning in `meta.warnings` and the item is marked `unknown`, never silently defaulted (L37 family).
CI runs the dashboard tests: the `python-lint` job installs pytest and runs `tests/dashboard`; `analyze.py --stage 30` exits 0 before the PR.
